# dsh-context-toolkit
> 简体中文 | **English** | Changelog
A DeepSeek Harness bundle whose single job is **keeping bulk output out of the conversation**.
It separates *raw bytes* from *conclusions*: commands run in a child process, files are analysed in
a sandbox, and long material is filed into a local knowledge base — while the conversation receives
only conclusions, excerpts and counts. A routing gate refuses, before execution, the calls that woul
d inevitably flood the transcript.
**No third-party runtime dependencies.** The knowledge base rides on Node's own `node:sqlite` (FTS5
included) and code execution uses interpreters already on the machine, so installing it pulls nothin
d) and code execution uses interpreters already on the machine, so installing it pulls nothing else.
## What it is for
| Problem | What this does |
| A command prints thousands of lines; you only need a count | `ctk_execute` runs it in a child proc

ess and returns the answer |
| A large file needs statistics, not a full read | `ctk_execute_file` k

eeps its bytes in the sandbox |
| Many commands, one question | `ctk_batch_execute` answers in one c

all with per-command status |
| A page or spec is read once and never reused | `ctk_index` files it;

`ctk_search` pulls excerpts on demand |
| `curl` / `wget` paste whole responses into the conversati

on | The routing gate refuses them and names the alternative |
| You cannot tell how much was saved
| `ctk_stats` reports the ledger; the settings page shows a live occupancy panel |

## TLS on a proxy-intercepted network
If every `ctk_fetch_and_index` fails with `UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE`, the machine sits behind

a
TLS-inspecting proxy and Node's built-in roots cannot verify what the proxy presents. `caPemPath`
names a PEM to trust instead.
`auto` (the default) points at `<DSH_HOME>/context-mode/ca/windows-roots.pem`. **This package does n

ot
ship that file** — it is a snapshot of the *host's own* root store, so on a fresh machine it simp

ly is
not there and fetching falls back to Node's default roots.
Settings → Context Toolkit shows a row under `caPemPath`:
- a badge saying whether the file exists (and its size), checked with a stat on page load — the bund

e (`tls.getCACertificates('system')`, ~500
certificates, ~820 KB) when pressed.
A bundle that already exists is never replaced on a single click: the first press asks, and only the
explicit confirmation overwrites it.
**What this does not do:** it exports the *system* store. If the proxy's root certificate was never
installed into that store — IT pushes it via group policy, for instance — the exported bundle still
will not verify the proxy. Install the root first, then export.
